title: Retain contradictory alignment outcomes as explicit motif evidence gaps

masterplan.active_gate: Gate 1 — Renovation, owner-directed Genesis and general computer assistance

scope: Tighten only the existing evolution motif evidence surface. If the same declared support pair carries both verified and rejected alignment records, preserve both records but expose the contradiction through evidence_gaps rather than allowing the verified edge to silently hide retained negative evidence. Do not add a second registry, graph authority, evaluator, promotion path, or Gate closure mechanism.

finding.inherited_gap: The historical blockers calculation and the first two selective ports used verified alignments for participation/connectivity but never surfaced a contradictory rejected result for the same support pair. A motif could therefore report an empty evidence-gap set while retaining both a verified and rejected claim over one pair.
finding.risk: Retained negative evidence would remain serialized but operationally invisible to consumers that correctly use evidence_gaps as the incompleteness/conflict summary. That weakens the Masterplan requirement to retain negative evidence and can make a disputed cross-repository relation look uncontested.

changes: Keep CrossRepositoryAlignment records and canonical serialization unchanged; conflicting evidence is retained, not rejected or overwritten.
Group alignment statuses by canonical support-digest pair inside the existing evidence_gaps calculation.
Emit one deterministic conflicting-alignment-status-<repository>-<repository> gap when a support pair has both verified and rejected outcomes.
Continue using verified edges for participation/connectivity while carrying the contradiction gap, so negative evidence does not erase independently verified paths.
Add a focused two-repository regression that proves verified and rejected records coexist and still produce a non-empty evidence gap.
gardener_notes: No new public concept, subsystem, store, registry, graph plane, receipt family, or evaluator was introduced.
The implementation stays inside daedalus.evolution, the existing Masterplan owner for corpus/motif contracts and retained negative evidence.
The branch was first synchronized with main@6dbf6053b0df6ce26717da1f15c555e102f8bec3 by a normal two-parent merge commit; no force update or history rewrite was used.
